---
title: "Methods"
---

**SiMR** (*Similarity-driven Multi-view Representation*) estimates a low-dimensional representation across $M$ views $\mathbf{X}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p_m}$ ($m = 1, \dots, M$) collected on $n$ subjects, generalizing classical Similarity-driven Multi-view Linear Reconstruction (**SiMLR**) [@avants2021] to support both linear and non-linear latent alignment. Every architecture in the family shares a common structural boundary—the Only Linear Encoder Entrypoint (OLEE)—and minimizes a generic composite objective combining within-view reconstruction, cross-view alignment, and approximate Stiefel regularization via `nsa_flow` [@avants2025]. @tbl-notation summarizes the mathematical notation.

| Term | Meaning |
|:---|:---|
| $\mathbf{X}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p_m}$ | Standardized data matrix for view $m \in \{1, \dots, M\}$ across $n$ subjects and $p_m$ features |
| $\bar{\mathbf{x}}_{m,\text{row}} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ | Per-subject row mean vector $\bar{x}_{i,m} = \frac{1}{p_m}\sum_{j=1}^{p_m} X_{ij,m}$, capturing global view amplitude (e.g., mean cortical thickness or brain size) |
| $\mathbf{V}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{p_m \times k}$ | First-layer linear loading matrix (OLEE basis) for view $m$, with latent rank $k \ll p_m$ |
| $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ | Linear entrypoint scores for view $m$, with constant input derivative $\nabla_{\mathbf{X}_m}\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{V}_m$ |
| $\mathbf{Z}_m = f_m(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}) \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ | Post-entrypoint latent embedding ($f_m = \mathrm{id}$ for linear `SiMLR` and `LEND` models; MLP or flow for `NED`/`NEDPP`/`Flow-SiMR-V`) |
| $g_m : \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^{p_m}$ | View-specific decoder mapping latent coordinates back to the ambient feature space $\mathbb{R}^{p_m}$ |
| $\mathbf{U}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ | Cross-view consensus target for view $m$, formed from neighbor views $\mathcal{N}(m)$ in alignment graph $\mathcal{G}$ |
| $w \in [0, 1]$ | Convex weight in `nsa_flow` balancing anchor fidelity $(1-w)$ against Stiefel orthogonality defect $w$ (default $w = 0.5$) |
| $D(\mathbf{V}_m) \in [0, 1]$ | Normalized Stiefel defect measuring distance of the trace-normalized Gram matrix $\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m / \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m)$ from $\frac{1}{k}\mathbf{I}_k$ |
: Core mathematical notation for the SiMR framework. {#tbl-notation}

---

## Generic Multi-View Objective

Given $M$ views $\{\mathbf{X}_m\}_{m=1}^M$ and an alignment graph $\mathcal{G} = (\{1, \dots, M\}, \mathcal{E})$, SiMR minimizes the generic multi-view objective:
$$
\min_{\{\mathbf{V}_m, f_m, g_m\}_{m=1}^M} \sum_{m=1}^M \Big[ \mathcal{L}_{\text{recon}}\!\big(\mathbf{X}_m,\, g_m(\mathbf{Z}_m)\big) + \lambda_{\text{sim}} \, \alpha_m \, \mathcal{L}_{\text{align}}\!\big(\mathbf{Z}_m,\, \mathbf{U}_m\big) + E_w\!\big(\mathbf{V}_m;\, \mathbf{V}_{m,0}\big) \Big] + \mathcal{R}\!\big(\{\mathbf{Z}_m\}\big),
$$ {#eq-generic-objective}
where $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ is the linear entrypoint projection, $\mathbf{Z}_m = f_m(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}})$ is the latent representation of view $m$, $\mathbf{U}_m = \operatorname{Consensus}(\{\mathbf{Z}_j\}_{j \in \mathcal{N}(m)})$ is the cross-view target aggregated over graph neighbors $\mathcal{N}(m)$, $\alpha_m \ge 0$ is the modality weight ($\sum_m \alpha_m = 1$), $E_w(\mathbf{V}_m; \mathbf{V}_{m,0})$ is the `nsa_flow` approximate Stiefel regularizer, and $\mathcal{R}(\{\mathbf{Z}_m\})$ denotes optional latent regularizers (such as the shared-private orthogonality penalty in `NEDPP` or the detached Gaussian prior log-likelihood in `Flow-SiMR-V`).

@tbl-method-instantiations summarizes how each of the nine benchmarked architectures instantiates @eq-generic-objective.

| Architecture | Input Layer $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}$ | Latent Map $f_m(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}})$ | Decoder $g_m(\mathbf{Z}_m)$ | Cross-View Term $\mathcal{L}_{\text{align}}$ | Basis Regularizer $E_w(\mathbf{V}_m)$ |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `PCA` | $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}$ (concatenated) | Identity ($\mathrm{id}$) | Linear ($\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{V}^\top$) | None ($\lambda_{\text{sim}} = 0$) | Exact SVD ($\mathbf{V}^\top \mathbf{V} = \mathbf{I}_k$, signed) |
| `NSAFlow-PCA` | $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}$ (concatenated) | Identity ($\mathrm{id}$) | Linear ($\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{V}^\top$) | None ($\lambda_{\text{sim}} = 0$) | `nsa_flow` ($w = 0.5$, $\mathbf{V} \ge 0$ or signed lobes) |
| `SiMLR` | $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ | Identity ($\mathrm{id}$) | Linear | Scale-profiled similarity | Armijo step + `nsa_flow` ($w = 0.5$) |
| `SiMLR-LBFGS` | $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ | Identity ($\mathrm{id}$) | Linear | Scale-profiled similarity | Two-loop L-BFGS + `nsa_flow` ($w = 0.5$) |
| `SiMLR-LBFGSB` | $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ | Identity ($\mathrm{id}$) | Linear | Scale-profiled similarity | Bound-constrained L-BFGS-B + `nsa_flow` ($w = 0.5$) |
| `LEND` | $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ | Identity ($\mathrm{id}$) | MLP $g_m(\mathbf{Z}_m)$ | Procrustes / cosine / log-cosh | Polar / `nsa_flow` retraction on $\mathbf{V}_m$ |
| `NED` | $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ | MLP $f_m(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}})$ | MLP $g_m(\mathbf{Z}_m)$ | Procrustes / cosine / log-cosh | Polar / `nsa_flow` retraction on $\mathbf{V}_m$ |
| `NEDPP` | $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ | Shared + private MLP | MLP $g_m([\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{sh}}, \mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{pr}}])$ | Procrustes + covariance penalty | Polar / `nsa_flow` retraction on $\mathbf{V}_m$ |
| `Flow-SiMR-V` | $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ | RealNVP $f_{\text{flow},m}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}})$ | Exact inverse $f_{\text{flow},m}^{-1}(\mathbf{Z}_m)\mathbf{V}_m^\top$ | Procrustes + detached Gaussian NLL | Polar / `nsa_flow` retraction on $\mathbf{V}_m$ |
: Instantiation of the generic SiMR objective (@eq-generic-objective) across the nine evaluated architectures. {#tbl-method-instantiations}

### Linear Attribution and Counterfactual Recourse at the OLEE Boundary

Restricting the first layer of every view to $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ guarantees two mathematical properties:

* **Constant per-feature attribution:** For subject $i$ and latent coordinate $l \in \{1, \dots, k\}$, the entrypoint score is $Z_{m,il} = \sum_{j=1}^{p_m} X_{m,ij} V_{m,jl}$. The derivative with respect to $\mathbf{X}_m$ is identically $\mathbf{V}_m$ for every subject. Patient-level feature attributions are given directly by the Hadamard product $\mathbf{x}_{m,i} \odot \mathbf{v}_{m,l}$ without post-hoc perturbation sampling.
* **Closed-form minimum-norm counterfactual shift:** For a unit-column-norm basis with $\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m \approx \mathbf{I}_k$, the minimum-$L_2$-norm feature shift $\delta \mathbf{x}_m^* \in \mathbb{R}^{p_m}$ required to produce a latent change $\Delta \mathbf{z}_m \in \mathbb{R}^k$ ($\delta \mathbf{x}_m \mathbf{V}_m = \Delta \mathbf{z}_m$) is the linear projection $\delta \mathbf{x}_m^* = \Delta \mathbf{z}_m (\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m)^{-1} \mathbf{V}_m^\top \approx \Delta \mathbf{z}_m \mathbf{V}_m^\top$.

---

## Approximate Stiefel Retraction via `nsa_flow`

When an outer optimization step proposes a candidate loading matrix $\mathbf{V}_{m,0} \in \mathbb{R}^{p_m \times k}$, `nsa_flow` minimizes the composite energy:
$$
\min_{\mathbf{V}_m \in \mathcal{C}} E_w(\mathbf{V}_m; \mathbf{V}_{m,0}) = (1 - w)\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{fid}}(\mathbf{V}_m, \mathbf{V}_{m,0}) + w\,D(\mathbf{V}_m),
$$ {#eq-nsa-energy}
where $\mathcal{C} = \{\mathbf{V} \in \mathbb{R}^{p_m \times k} : \mathbf{V} \ge 0\}$ when non-negativity is active (`positivity="positive"`, or $\mathbb{R}^{p_m \times k}$ when unconstrained `positivity="either"`), and $w \in [0, 1]$ is a convex balancing weight.

### Dimensionless Energy Terms

Both terms in @eq-nsa-energy are dimensionless and bounded on $[0, 1]$:

1. **Fidelity term ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{fid}}$):** Measures the relative Frobenius distance to the candidate update $\mathbf{V}_{m,0}$,
   $$
   \mathcal{L}_{\text{fid}}(\mathbf{V}_m, \mathbf{V}_{m,0}) = \frac{\|\mathbf{V}_m - \mathbf{V}_{m,0}\|_F^2}{\|\mathbf{V}_{m,0}\|_F^2},
   $$
   which equals $0$ at $\mathbf{V}_m = \mathbf{V}_{m,0}$ and $1$ at $\mathbf{V}_m = \mathbf{0}$.
2. **Normalized Stiefel defect ($D(\mathbf{V}_m)$):** Let $\mathbf{S}_m = \mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m$, $t_m = \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{S}_m) = \|\mathbf{V}_m\|_F^2$, and $\mathbf{G}_m = \mathbf{S}_m / t_m$ be the trace-normalized Gram matrix. The normalized Stiefel defect is
   $$
   D(\mathbf{V}_m) = \frac{1}{1 - 1/k}\left\|\mathbf{G}_m - \frac{1}{k}\mathbf{I}_k\right\|_F^2 = \frac{1}{1 - 1/k}\Bigg[\underbrace{\sum_{l \neq r} G_{m,lr}^2}_{\text{decorrelation}} + \underbrace{\sum_{l=1}^k \Big(G_{m,ll} - \frac{1}{k}\Big)^2}_{\text{norm balance}}\Bigg].
   $$ {#eq-stiefel-defect}
   $D(\mathbf{V}_m)$ vanishes if and only if the columns of $\mathbf{V}_m$ are mutually orthogonal and have equal norms ($\mathbf{V}_m \in \mathbb{R}_{>0} \cdot \mathrm{St}(k, p_m)$). Because $D(\mathbf{V}_m) = \frac{1}{1 - 1/k}\big(\frac{1}{\operatorname{EffRank}(\mathbf{V}_m)} - \frac{1}{k}\big)$, any rank-deficient matrix of rank $r < k$ incurs a strictly positive floor $D(\mathbf{V}_m) \ge \frac{1/r - 1/k}{1 - 1/k}$. By Euler's identity for degree-zero homogeneous functions, $\langle \nabla_{\mathbf{V}_m} D(\mathbf{V}_m), \mathbf{V}_m \rangle = 0$ identically, so $D(\mathbf{V}_m)$ rotates and balances columns without modifying total matrix scale $\|\mathbf{V}_m\|_F$.

### Structural Sparsity and Weight Selection ($w = 0.5$)

For a non-negative matrix $\mathbf{V}_m \ge 0$, two columns $\mathbf{v}_{m,l}$ and $\mathbf{v}_{m,r}$ satisfy $\langle \mathbf{v}_{m,l}, \mathbf{v}_{m,r} \rangle = 0$ if and only if their non-zero supports are disjoint: $\operatorname{supp}(\mathbf{v}_{m,l}) \cap \operatorname{supp}(\mathbf{v}_{m,r}) = \emptyset$. Consequently:

* **The $1 - 1/k$ structural sparsity bound:** Under $\mathbf{V}_m \ge 0$ and $D(\mathbf{V}_m) \to 0$, each feature can load on at most one of the $k$ columns. Across $k p_m$ entries, at most $p_m$ entries are non-zero, yielding a theoretical baseline sparsity of
  $$
  \operatorname{Sparsity}(\mathbf{V}_m) \ge 1 - \frac{p_m}{k p_m} = 1 - \frac{1}{k},
  $$ {#eq-k-sparsity}
  which evaluates to $50.0\%$ at $k = 2$, $66.7\%$ at $k = 3$, $80.0\%$ at $k = 5$, and $91.7\%$ at $k = 12$. When unconstrained signed bases are fitted (`positivity="either"`), columns satisfy $\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m = \mathbf{I}_k$ via signed cancellation with $0\%$ sparsity.
* **Weight behavior ($w$):** When $w < 0.20$, the cross-view alignment gradient dominates orthogonality, collapsing columns onto collinear directions ($\operatorname{EffRank}(\mathbf{V}_m) \to 2.0$ of $3$ at $w = 0.01$ on `ADNI-MCI`, with defect $D = 0.244$). At $w = 1$, the fidelity term $(1 - w)\mathcal{L}_{\text{fid}}$ vanishes, leaving scale unconstrained and enforcing a rigid combinatorial partition where shared biological hubs cannot participate in multiple pathways. Setting $w = 0.5$ as default (capping hard-manifold requests at $w_{\max} = 0.95$) achieves full effective rank ($\operatorname{EffRank} = 3.00$, $D \le 6 \times 10^{-4}$) in $O(p_m k^2)$ operations per iteration without inner-loop SVD or QR factorizations.

### The 3-Stage Support-Masked Polish and Sign-Gauge Resolution

When quantile sparseness $q$ is specified, `nsa_flow` executes a 3-stage support-masked Riemannian polish (@fig-nsa-flow-polish-pipeline):

1. **Stage 1 (Full-Support Riemannian Flow):** Solves an unconstrained Riemannian flow minimizing $E_w(\mathbf{Y}; \mathbf{Y}_0)$ on the Stiefel manifold across all $p_m$ features, identifying the dominant multi-modal spectral subspace.
2. **Stage 2 (Support Masking & Per-Column Sign-Gauge Resolution):** For each column $\mathbf{y}_l \in \mathbb{R}^{p_m}$ and target active count $s_m = \max(1, \operatorname{round}((1 - q_m)p_m))$, the order-statistic threshold $\tau_{m,l} = |y_{(s_m+1),l}|$ is calculated. Under `only_if_denser=True`, if a column already contains more than $q_m$ zeros, its natural zeros are retained. Otherwise, a binary support mask $\mathbf{M}_m \in \{0, 1\}^{p_m \times k}$ is defined by $M_{jl} = \mathbf{1}(|y_{jl}| > \tau_{m,l})$.
   
   Prior to non-negative projection or clamping ($\mathbf{V} \ge 0$), the per-column sign gauge is resolved by evaluating positive vs. negative $L_2$ mass survivor:
   $$
   \mathbf{v}_{m,l} \leftarrow -\mathbf{v}_{m,l} \quad \text{if } \|\max(0, -\mathbf{v}_{m,l})\|_2 > \|\max(0, \mathbf{v}_{m,l})\|_2.
   $$ {#eq-sign-gauge}
   This reflection ensures that the dominant biological activation is oriented positively before non-negative clamping $\mathbf{V}_m \leftarrow \max(0, \mathbf{V}_m)$.
3. **Stage 3 (Masked Stiefel Polish):** With the support mask $\mathbf{M}_m$ fixed, `nsa_flow` executes Riemannian optimization with gradients pinned strictly to the active coordinates ($\nabla_{\mathbf{Y}} E \odot \mathbf{M}_m$). This step restores column orthogonality and norm balance without leaking weight into zeroed background features, ensuring $D(\mathbf{V}_m) \le 10^{-4}$ alongside exact feature sparsity.

## Controlling Component 1 Sparsity: Row-Mean Control, Deterministic ICA, and Quantile `sparseness`

When applying non-negative basis learning to neuroimaging or multi-omics matrices under standard column-centering and PCA initialization, each subject possesses a non-zero row mean across features:
$$
\bar{x}_{i,m} = \frac{1}{p_m}\sum_{j=1}^{p_m} X_{ij,m}, \qquad \mathbf{X}_m = \bar{\mathbf{x}}_{m,\text{row}}\mathbf{1}_{p_m}^\top + \tilde{\mathbf{X}}_m, \quad \tilde{\mathbf{X}}_m \mathbf{1}_{p_m} = \mathbf{0}.
$$ {#eq-row-mean-decomp}
In structural brain MRI, $\bar{x}_{i,m}$ represents subject $i$'s mean cortical thickness or parenchymal volume across all $p_m$ anatomical parcels. Because regional volumes and thicknesses covary positively across the cortex, the sample covariance matrix $\frac{1}{n}\mathbf{X}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m$ has predominantly positive entries. By the Perron–Frobenius theorem, its leading eigenvector $\mathbf{v}_{m,1}^{\text{PCA}}$ is dense and strictly positive ($\mathbf{v}_{m,1}^{\text{PCA}} \approx \mathbf{1}_{p_m}/\sqrt{p_m}$), while subsequent eigenvectors $\mathbf{v}_{m,2}^{\text{PCA}}, \dots, \mathbf{v}_{m,k}^{\text{PCA}}$ contain positive and negative entries to satisfy orthogonality.

Clamping PCA initialization to $\mathbf{V}_m \ge 0$ leaves $\mathbf{v}_{m,1}$ dense ($35.8\%$ sparsity on `ADNI-MCI` at $k = 3$) while forcing Components $2, \dots, k$ into the remaining parcels ($76.6\%$ sparsity). Because $D(\mathbf{V}_m)$ in @eq-stiefel-defect penalizes only between-column inner products and column-norm imbalance, any partition of features into $k$ disjoint subsets of unit norm achieves $D(\mathbf{V}_m) = 0$, including asymmetric partitions.

We examine three complementary mechanisms in `PySiMLR` to control Component 1 density:

1. **In-fold row-mean control (double-centering):** Projecting each matrix onto the orthogonal complement of $\mathbf{1}_{p_m}$ ($\tilde{\mathbf{X}}_m = \mathbf{X}_m - \bar{\mathbf{x}}_{m,\text{row}}\mathbf{1}_{p_m}^\top$) removes the rank-1 global subject mode prior to optimization.
2. **Deterministic spatial ICA initialization (`initialization_type="ica"`):** Given deterministic singular vectors $\mathbf{V}_{m,\text{SVD}} \in \mathbb{R}^{p_m \times k}$, parallel `FastICA` (`fun="logcosh"`, seeded with $\mathbf{W}_0 = \mathbf{I}_k$) rotates the basis toward spatially localized directions before retraction. Combining row-mean removal and ICA initialization equalizes sparsity across columns ($66\%\text{--}69\%$ at $k=3$), though discarding global atrophy covariance reduces out-of-sample cognitive prediction on `ADNI-MCI`.
3. **Quantile `sparseness` operator ($q \in (0, 1)$, default $0.5$, operating points $0.5$ and $0.8$):** Following @avants2021, we define three primary operating points:
   - **$q = \text{None}$ (Unsparsified Baseline):** Relies strictly on `nsa_flow` Stiefel regularization and non-negativity to enforce structural sparsity ($1 - 1/k$).
   - **$q = 0.5$ (Balanced Discovery):** Soft-thresholds the lowest $50\%$ of weights per column, eliminating diffuse background noise while preserving secondary pathway hubs.
   - **$q = 0.8$ (Focal Diagnostic Biomarker Panel Design):** Soft-thresholds $80\%$ of features per column, isolating compact panels of the top $20\%$ focal biomarkers (such as 9 DKT cortical parcels or 20 diagnostic genes) for translational clinical assays.

## Cross-View Consensus Topologies and Bipartite Clinical Alignment

The cross-view alignment term $\mathcal{L}_{\text{align}}(\mathbf{Z}_m, \mathbf{U}_m)$ pulls each view's latent representation $\mathbf{Z}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ toward a view-specific consensus target $\mathbf{U}_m$ constructed from its neighbor set $\mathcal{N}(m)$ in graph $\mathcal{G}$. Prior to averaging across views, columns are sign-aligned (`align_column_signs`) against a running reference, followed by Gram–Schmidt, SVD, or 10-step Newton–Schulz orthogonalization.

SiMR supports three consensus topologies:

1. **Pooled star topology (`topology="star"`):** Every view aligns to the global consensus of all $M$ views, $\mathcal{N}(m) = \{1, \dots, M\}$.
2. **Leave-one-out topology (`topology="loo"`):** View $m$ aligns strictly against the consensus of the remaining $M - 1$ views, $\mathcal{N}(m) = \{j \neq m\}$, preventing a high-dimensional view from dominating via self-correlation.
3. **Directed and bipartite graph topology (`topology="graph"`):** In clinical cohorts where $M - 1$ predictor views $\{\mathbf{X}_1, \dots, \mathbf{X}_{M-1}\}$ (e.g., three structural MRI views in `ADNI-MCI`) are accompanied during training by a supervisory clinical or cognitive view $\mathbf{X}_M$ (e.g., the 11-scale cognitive battery), aligning the MRI views with each other allows global brain size and healthy aging covariance to dominate the leading components. Specifying the bipartite neighbor sets
   $$
   \mathcal{N}(m) = \{M\} \quad (m = 1, \dots, M-1), \qquad \mathcal{N}(M) = \{1, \dots, M-1\}
   $$ {#eq-bipartite-graph}
   routes all cross-view alignment during training between the imaging views and the cognitive battery (`Protocol B`). At test time, View $M$ is withheld (`eval_view_indices` $= \{1, \dots, M-1\}$) and out-of-sample predictions are formed strictly from the test imaging views:
   $$
   \mathbf{Z}_{\text{test},\text{lin}} = \big[\mathbf{X}_{1,\text{test}}\mathbf{V}_1, \dots, \mathbf{X}_{M-1,\text{test}}\mathbf{V}_{M-1}\big], \qquad \hat{\mathbf{U}}_{\text{test}} = \frac{1}{M - 1}\sum_{m=1}^{M-1} f_m(\mathbf{X}_{m,\text{test}}\mathbf{V}_m).
   $$

---

## Non-Linear Decoding (`LEND`) and Detached-Prior Normalizing Flows (`Flow-SiMR-V`)

To capture non-linear relationships between the shared latent state and the observed measurements while preserving the linear input boundary $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$, SiMR provides two primary non-linear extensions:

* **Linear Encoder, Non-linear Decoder (`LEND`):** Keeps the encoder strictly linear ($f_m = \mathrm{id}$, so $\mathbf{Z}_m = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$) and places a multi-layer perceptron in the decoder $g_m : \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^{p_m}$. Because the encoder has only $p_m k$ parameters regularized by $E_w(\mathbf{V}_m)$, `LEND` avoids the high-dimensional encoder overfitting that occurs when MLP layers are inserted inside the encoder (`NED` and `NEDPP`) when $p_m \gg n$.
* **Bijective Normalizing Flow Downstream of OLEE (`Flow-SiMR-V`):** Applies an invertible RealNVP affine coupling flow $f_{\text{flow},m} : \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^k$ to the linear projection $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$, with exact inverse reconstruction $\hat{\mathbf{X}}_m = f_{\text{flow},m}^{-1}(\mathbf{Z}_m)\mathbf{V}_m^\top$.

### Detached-Prior Subspace Decoupling in `Flow-SiMR-V`

If the standard Gaussian prior negative log-likelihood
$$
\mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}; f_{\text{flow},m}) = \frac{1}{2n}\sum_{i=1}^n \|f_{\text{flow},m}(\mathbf{z}_{m,\text{lin},i})\|_2^2 - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \log\left|\det \frac{\partial f_{\text{flow},m}}{\partial \mathbf{z}_{m,\text{lin}}}(\mathbf{z}_{m,\text{lin},i})\right|
$$
is backpropagated directly into the rectangular basis $\mathbf{V}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{p_m \times k}$ ($k \ll p_m$), minimizing $\frac{1}{2}\|\mathbf{Z}_m\|_2^2 \approx \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m)$ with respect to $\mathbf{V}_m$ rotates $\mathbf{V}_m$ onto the trailing (smallest-eigenvalue) noise eigenvectors of $\mathbf{X}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m$, because the Jacobian determinant accounts only for volume changes inside $\mathbb{R}^k$. `Flow-SiMR-V` prevents this collapse by detaching $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}$ at the input to the Gaussian prior loss—evaluating $\mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}\big(f_{\text{flow},m}(\operatorname{sg}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}))\big)$ where $\operatorname{sg}(\cdot)$ is the stop-gradient operator—so that $\mathbf{V}_m$ is updated exclusively by cross-view alignment and reconstruction fidelity while $f_{\text{flow},m}$ warps the resulting $k$-dimensional coordinates toward the Gaussian prior.

---

## Evaluation Protocol: The Three Probes and Statistical Inference

All benchmark experiments follow leak-free evaluation rules:

1. **In-fold preprocessing:** Feature standardization (`StandardScaler`), column completeness filtering ($\ge 98\%$), demographic residualization (`AGE`, `PTGENDER`, `PTEDUCAT` on `ADNI-MCI`), and optional per-subject row-mean removal are fitted strictly inside each training split and applied to the held-out test split.
2. **Evaluation Probes and Ground-Truth Recovery:** We evaluate models under four complementary operational lenses:
   - **Probe 1: Subspace Linear Probe on $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}$ (Rotation-Invariant):** Ridge regression predicting held-out targets from concatenated first-layer scores $[\mathbf{X}_{1,\text{test}}\mathbf{V}_1, \dots, \mathbf{X}_{M,\text{test}}\mathbf{V}_M]$. Because $\operatorname{span}(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}\mathbf{M}) = \operatorname{span}(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V})$, this probe measures whether the learned subspace captures the overall disease variance.
   - **Probe 2: Single-Axis Random Forest Probe on $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}$ (Coordinate-Sensitive):** Random Forest decision tree ensemble predicting held-out targets from $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{V}$. Decision trees split on single coordinates ($z_j \le \theta$). When biological factors are diagonally rotated across multiple axes (as in PCA), Random Forest performance drops precipitously. This probe directly verifies whether learned coordinates are aligned with true biological axes.
   - **Probe 3: Shared Patient Consensus Probe on $\mathbf{U}$:** Ridge or SVM classifier predicting held-out targets from the fused $k$-dimensional patient consensus embedding $\hat{\mathbf{U}}_{\text{test}}$, evaluating multi-modal compression.
   - **Ground-Truth Support Recovery & Defect:** On synthetic regimes with known ground truth $(\mathbf{U}^*, \mathbf{V}_m^*)$, we evaluate Canonical Mean Correlation ($CMC$ between $\hat{\mathbf{U}}$ and $\mathbf{U}^*$), sparse support Jaccard $F_1$, and scale-invariant Stiefel defect $D(\mathbf{V}_m) \in [0, 1]$.
3. **Block-level non-parametric inference:** Following @Demsar2006, multi-seed replicates are averaged within each $(\text{Dataset}, \text{Model})$ cell (`build_ranking_blocks` in `src/pysimlr/benchmarks/deep_ranking.py`) so that repeated seeds are treated as replicates of a dataset rather than independent tasks. Across the $B = 12$ independent dataset blocks and $k = 9$ models, we report the Friedman $\chi_F^2$ test, the Iman–Davenport $F_F$ statistic [@Iman1980], the two-tailed Nemenyi Critical Difference ($CD = 3.468$ at $\alpha = 0.05$) [@Nemenyi1963], and pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm step-down adjustment [@Holm1979] alongside exact sign-flip permutation $p$-values.
